title: an untrusted foreign call's result may not be consumed as a raw value in an expression: the lowered form is a Result, not a number
notes: specification/failures.mdx §Foreign Exceptions (Locked): 'Calling any TypeScript, JavaScript, or other foreign runtime implementation MUST add the distinguished checked `panic` case by default. This applies even when the foreign declaration omits throws.' `parseIntegerUnchecked` omits `@throws`, so `parseIntegerUnchecked(text)` is a `Result<number, Panic>`, and `Result<number, Panic> + 1` is not arithmetic. SMITHERS1301 is the compiler saying so: it really did produce a Result at 5:10 and nothing consumed it. SMITHERS1507 IS NO LONGER REPORTED HERE, and that is the change this note exists to record. The lowerability predicate in poc/src/language/semantic.ts had two branches, and this case pinned the second: `unsafeUse = annotation !== "never" && foreignResultIsUsedAsValue(call)`. That branch was a PLACEMENT rule wearing a provenance rule's name — it existed because the `Result.try(...)` wrapper had to be hoisted in front of the statement, which is the same withdrawn constraint specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions retired for postfix `!` (DECISIONS.md §Typed failures, 2026-08-30). The wrapper is an expression and stays where it was written, so the branch and its helper are deleted. What SMITHERS1507 still means is narrower and is entirely about PROVENANCE: an unstable foreign callee the compiler cannot read once, or a receiver that is already an unchecked foreign value. Its surviving first branch is pinned by a-foreign-factory-result-invoked-before-it-is-unwrapped-is-rejected, which is why that case and this one were written separately in the first place — an implementation can lose either branch without losing the other, and here one of them was deliberately removed. The remedy the old message named is unchanged and still demonstrated by a-foreign-callable-wrapped-in-a-local-adapter-is-accepted: unwrap or match the checked result, then compute.

xfail.reason: the fork still reports SMITHERS1507@5:10 beside SMITHERS1301@5:10. Its lowerability predicate in compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt keeps the branch the reference deleted — the one that refused a checked foreign result USED AS A VALUE, which was a placement constraint of the hoisted `Result.try(...)` wrapper and not a provenance fact. FAIL-CLOSED: the fork reports one code more than the reference and compiles nothing either way, so the marker holds no fail-open. MEASURED on both backends with `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --filter 09-foreign-calls`. The marker retires when the fork drops the same branch; its surviving first branch (an unstable foreign callee) must keep firing, and a-foreign-factory-result-invoked-before-it-is-unwrapped-is-rejected is the case that proves it did.
xfail.doc: specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions: the failure exit is an expression in every position, so a lowering that has to be hoisted is no longer a reason to refuse a placement.
